historical_basis: Kent28pp949-951; Berg1988 extract: northern Imerina royal court distinct from Antananarivo before consolidation. Two native cells approximate the northern royal sector; court coordinates overlap the scale of neighbouring native cells, no precise cadastral boundary claimed. Irrigated rice, cattle, textile/metal craft, exchanges and royal armed retainers.

Kent28p950-951: western Imerina royal power not conquered until later1790s. Native western royal-sector envelope, not a new pixel-level palace boundary. Rice/cattle, weaving/workshops and court/market relations.

Kent28pp945-947: northern royal line and organisation borrowed from Boina, tribute attested before1776; autonomy preserved with native tributary pact. No claimed accession date installed. Native offshore islands remain with their mainland provinces.

Kent28pp943-947: northwestern Sakalava court, markets and tribute networks, distinct from Menabe and Merina. Royal nucleus and adjoining directly associated western hinterland; not wholesale annexation of every tributary. Trading and military organisation; no commercial-insurance or gun-manufacturing technology.

Kent28pp943-947: northwestern Sakalava court, markets and tribute networks, distinct from Menabe and Merina. Royal nucleus and adjoining directly associated western hinterland; not wholesale annexation of every tributary. Trading and military organisation; no commercial-insurance or gun-manufacturing technology.
Kent28pp945-946: autonomous upper-Sofia/Mandritsara communities, no central kingdom or regular tribute. Rural farming/cattle/craft capabilities, no fictional monarch.

Kent28pp955-957,944: local filohany and autonomous clans persist after confederation; coastal armed commerce, royal influence and disputed Boina tribute do not equal uniform administration. Plural engine aggregate, not a single new national monarchy. Benyowsky/French coastal installations remain a documented local limitation.

Kent28pp951-952: fortified Alaotra communities, potters, bridge and trade; no central authority. Historical Boina tribute not converted into direct provincial rule or a native centralised-subject pact.

Kent28pp951-952: Ankay forest-route communities and fortified villages under local mpifehy; later short-lived kingship not projected automatically into1776. Indigenous markets/textile/metal craft and regional exchange.

Kent28p951: western Imamo and Betafo/Andratsay powers submitted only during later Merina consolidation. Explicit plural aggregate of distinct local authorities, potentially separated by royal cores; no unified ethnic monarchy claimed.

Kent28pp940-945: separate western Sakalava monarchy, riverine royal framework and stock/market economy; northern Boina distinct. Native coastal/interior envelope between western interfaces, not all ethnic Sakalava treated as direct subjects.

Kent28pp940-945: separate western Sakalava monarchy, riverine royal framework and stock/market economy; northern Boina distinct. Native coastal/interior envelope between western interfaces, not all ethnic Sakalava treated as direct subjects.
Kent28pp947-949: royal formation afterc1750, submission to Merina c1800. Northern Betsileo three-cell court envelope, no forced1776 subject status.

Kent28pp947-949: eighteenth-century Andriamanalina court, royal rice/cattle reforms and diplomacy/armed retainers. Extent of hegemony and its chronology not treated as direct possession of all Betsileo.
Kent28pp947-948: independent Betsileo court, national militia and rice reforms, resistance to later Merina demands. Court retained separately from Isandra, no exact1776 ruler invented.

Kent28pp947-948: southern Betsileo royal formation distinct from Lalangina/Isandra, neighbouring Bara. Native southern highland envelope; internal/later Isandra hegemony not certified as permanent direct rule.
Kent28pp952-953: plural forest communities outside distinct Ikongo royal centre, never one all-Tanala state. Native northern forest sector, rural/craft capabilities without national institutions.

Kent28pp952-953: Zafirambo royal centre recorded since1668, local law/ritual specialists and fortified royal rock, conflicts with Antemoro. Rice/cattle/craft and royal guard model; no later Merina alliance at start.
Kent28pp955,958: distinct southeastern coastal royal formation outside Betsimisaraka/Merina, around Mananjary. Small native littoral envelope, detailed dynasty/chronology unresolved.

Kent28pp923-926,953,958: Matitana coastal royal society, sorabe specialists, rice/overseas commerce and royal conflict with Ikongo. National culture malagasy is a native proxy; no POP religion conversion or blanket Islamic state imposed.
Kent28pp957-958: Ambaky/Farafangana royal power and maritime trade, distinct from Antemoro and Antesaka. Two native coastal-interface cells, no exact succession date asserted.

Kent28pp957-958: Nosipandra/Vangaindrano royal line and rice economy; independent political formation before later Merina expansion. Native coastal sector, not precise final boundaries under late18c rulers.

Kent28pp958-959: many small local kings in Ambolo/Mandrare, no unified large Antanosy state. Native southeast envelope; FortDauphin settlement attempt1767-1770 not projected as continuous French territorial administration.

Kent28pp959-960: Karimbola autonomy and weakening Zafimanara confederation, continued local leaders, no whole southern peninsula ruled from Imerina. Pastoral/craft capabilities, no specific collapse date forced.

Kent28pp939-941: four independent Mahafaly kingdoms and clan authorities, not a single national monarchy. Native southwest strip aggregated at available scale; internal royal authority acknowledged, unresolved internal borders not invented.

Kent28p932 and regional southwest discussion: Andrevola royal power in Fiherenana valley distinct from Sakalava-Maroserana. Coastal valley/river envelope, not uniform control over all southern Masikoro communities.

Kent28pp953-955: multiple Zafimanely/clan kings and strong local councils, no single sovereign over all Ibara. Plural political aggregate, not absence of chiefs; pastoral/rural craft, no post1800 consolidation.

Kent28pp960-964: separate island sultanates and rival local courts, no Merina authority. One inherited native province covers the archipelago; explicit plural autonomous aggregate rather than a unified Comorian state. Ports/craft/commerce model, not a historical national constitution.
